newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell Singapore to cut June refinery output.
newsitem.headline: Shell Singapore to cut June refinery output.

text.p: Shell Singapore will cut its output in the second half of June to achieve an average June output of 57,000 tonne-per-day (TPD) from the June average to date of 59,000 TPD, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.

"During the month of June 1997 Shell Pulau Bukom refinery production has to date been running at around 59,000 TPD. As a response to market condition, the plan is to achieve an average of 57,000 TPD for the month," the spokeswoman said.
"This will entail production cuts in the second half of the month."
The production cuts are expected to amount to 4,000 TPD (28,000 barrel per day) or about seven percent of Shell's total refining capacity.

Sources said Shell may extend the cuts in to July if the current poor margin and high stock situation does not improve. Margins are currently volatile with negative levels seen in some days over the past month.
